knowledge-base.name: rag-http-api
knowledge-base.description: HTTP REST API for the ClaudeBoost RAG server. Any script, tool, or service can call RAG without MCP by sending plain JSON requests to the server running on localhost. Same data as the MCP tools, different transport.

when-to-use.use-case: Scripts that need semantic search but can't use MCP (shell scripts, Python scripts, CI jobs)
Other AI tools or agent frameworks that speak HTTP but not MCP
Debugging RAG results directly with curl
Building tools on top of ClaudeBoost RAG from outside Claude Code

not-for.item: Inside Claude Code sessions — use the HTTP API directly (POST /search, POST /context, GET /status). No MCP required.
Production external traffic — the server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, no auth, localhost only

prerequisites.step: Start the RAG server: run /rag in your Claude Code session
Wait for model load (~30-60s on first start). The /status endpoint returns 503 until ready.
prerequisites.note: No authentication required. The server only accepts connections from localhost.

endpoint.description: Check if the server is up and the embedding model is loaded.

response-ready.field: object with chunk/file counts per scope (knowledge, agents, memories)
map of project paths that have been indexed for codebase search

endpoint.description: Semantic search across ClaudeBoost knowledge bases, agents, or a project codebase. Returns the top matching chunks ranked by relevance score.

request-fields.field: Which index to search. Valid values: "all" (knowledge + agents + memories), "knowledge" (knowledge/*.xml files), "agents" (agents/*.xml files), "memories" (user memory files), "codebase" (project source code, requires project_path), "research" (indexed URLs/PDFs, requires workspace_path), "project-docs" (project markdown/rst docs indexed via POST /index_docs, requires project_path)
Absolute path to the project root. Required when scope="codebase".
Absolute path to the workspace directory. Required when scope="research".
"vector" for semantic search, "graph" for structural neighbours (codebase only)

response-fields.field: array of matching chunks
chunk text
file path the chunk came from
relevance score (0.0-1.0)
additional metadata (scope, chunk type, etc.)
present only on failure

endpoint.example-curl:
# Search all knowledge and agent files curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "how to handle errors in Python", "scope": "knowledge"}'
# Search a project codebase curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "authentication middleware", "scope": "codebase", "project_path": "/home/user/myproject", "limit": 10 }'
endpoint.example-python:
import requests
# Search knowledge files resp = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:8612/search", json={ "query": "parameterized SQL queries", "scope": "knowledge", "limit": 3, }) for r in resp.json()["results"]: print(f"{r['score']:.2f} {r['source']}") print(r["content"][:200]) print()
# Search a project codebase with graph mode resp = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:8612/search", json={ "query": "UserRepository", "scope": "codebase", "project_path": "/home/user/myproject", "mode": "graph", })

endpoint.description:
Build the same curated context that POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/context builds for agent spawning: relevant knowledge files, agent definitions, and (if a project is indexed) matching code chunks. Also includes workspace-scoped research (Tier 3c) when workspace_path is provided. Use this to prime an LLM with the right background before a task.
Context tiers assembled: - Tier 0: Agent definition - Tier 1: Guardrails (security, observability, coding-standards) - Tier 2: Agent-declared knowledge - Tier 3: Semantic knowledge search (stack-boosted if project_path provided) - Tier 3c: Workspace research (if workspace_path provided and research index exists) - Tier 4: Codebase search + graph neighbours + community summaries (if project indexed)

request-fields.field: Agent name or role, e.g. "explore", "debug", "architect". Used to find matching agent definitions and weight the knowledge selection.
Short description of the task. Used as the search query to find relevant context.
Token budget for the returned context. Raised from 4000 to 6000 to accommodate new tiers (Tier 3c workspace research, stack-boosted Tier 3 queries).
Context depth. "lightweight" (agent def only, skips guardrails and Tier 3c), "standard" (all tiers), "full" (standard + verify gate instructions).
Absolute path to an indexed project. Enables Tier 4 codebase search and auto-detects the project stack to boost Tier 3 knowledge queries.

Absolute path to the task workspace directory (e.g. "$CLAUDEBOOST_HOME/workspace/ASC-1199"). When provided and a research index exists (built by POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/index_research or /research-task), Tier 3c injects up to 400 tokens of task-specific research docs into context.

response-fields.field: full agent definition text
array of knowledge/codebase/research chunks with source, tier, score
approximate token count of the full context package
chunk counts per tier: guardrails, declared, search, workspace_research, codebase, community_summaries
present only on failure

endpoint.example-curl:
# Basic context call curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/context \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "agent": "debug", "task_description": "fix authentication bug in Python FastAPI app", "project_path": "/home/user/myproject" }'
# Full context with workspace research (Tier 3c) curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/context \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "agent": "workflow", "task_description": "implement email notifications for address changes", "project_path": "C:/Development/MyApp", "workspace_path": "C:/YourClaudeBoostPath/workspace/TASK-1234", "max_tokens": 8000 }'
endpoint.example-python:
import urllib.request, json
def get_context(agent, task, project_path=None, workspace_path=None, max_tokens=6000): body = json.dumps({ "agent": agent, "task_description": task, "max_tokens": max_tokens, **({"project_path": project_path} if project_path else {}), **({"workspace_path": workspace_path} if workspace_path else {}), }).encode() req = urllib.request.Request( "http://127.0.0.1:8612/context", data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r: return json.loads(r.read())
ctx = get_context( "workflow-agent", "implement address change email notifications in ASP.NET Core", project_path="C:/Development/MyApp", workspace_path="C:/YourClaudeBoostPath/workspace/TASK-1234", ) print(f"{ctx['total_tokens_approx']} tokens | tiers: {ctx['tier_summary']}")
endpoint.note: workspace_path enables Tier 3c only when a research index exists at workspace_path/.rag-index/research/. Build it with /research-task (auto-seeded from ticket entities, or pass URLs for manual curation — add --approve for the interactive approval gate). Then pass workspace_path to /context and the research loads automatically.

endpoint.description: Index (or reindex) a project's source code into the Project RAG codebase index. After indexing, the project is searchable via POST /search with scope="codebase". Also builds the GraphRAG structural index (imports, inheritance chains).

request-fields.field: Absolute path to the project root to index.
When true, re-embeds all files even if they haven't changed. Useful if the embedding model was upgraded. Can take 30+ minutes on large projects — confirm before using.

response-fields.field: number of files successfully embedded and stored
number of files skipped (hash unchanged)
number of files that errored — check errors[] if nonzero
array of {file, type, message} entries, present only when files_failed > 0
total indexing time in seconds
number of graph edges built (imports/inheritance)
number of graph edges successfully resolved

endpoint.note: files_failed > 0 is the signal that something went wrong. Zero failures = healthy index. Retry failed embed_error entries once with force=true before escalating.

endpoint.description:
Index (or reindex) a project's markdown and reStructuredText documentation files into a per-project docs collection. After indexing, the docs are searchable via POST /search with scope="project-docs" and are automatically injected as Tier 4d in POST /context calls when a project is provided.
The docs index is separate from the codebase index (POST /index). It covers .md and .rst files only, excluding build dirs, node_modules, venv, .git, etc. Incremental: files are skipped if their content hash hasn't changed.

request-fields.field: Absolute path to the project root to scan for docs.
Optional list of specific file paths to index. When provided, only those files are indexed instead of scanning the full project tree.
When true, re-embeds all docs even if content is unchanged. Use after switching embedding models.

response-fields.field: number of doc files embedded and stored
number of files skipped (hash unchanged or empty)
number of files that errored
total chunks added to the collection
total .md/.rst files found in the project
absolute path to the ChromaDB store for this project's docs
total indexing time in milliseconds

endpoint.example-curl:
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/index_docs \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"project_path": "/home/user/myproject"}'
# Force rebuild (after model upgrade) curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/index_docs \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"project_path": "/home/user/myproject", "force": true}'
endpoint.note: The docs index lives at <project>/.rag-index/docs/chroma/. It is built and queried independently of the codebase index (<project>/workspace/.rag-index/). Running POST /index does NOT build the docs index — you must call POST /index_docs separately. POST /context injects docs results automatically as Tier 4d (up to 300 tokens) when project_path is provided and a docs index exists.

error-responses.error: {"error": "Server is still initializing, retry in a moment."}

wait-for-ready-pattern.description: Poll /status until the model is loaded before making search or context calls.
